page: Hetzner Cloud cpx21 is an entry-tier virtual machine hosted on the QEMU hypervisor using standard x86_64 architecture. The instance is provisioned with 3 shared AMD EPYC virtual cores running at a 2.0 GHz clock speed, accompanied by 4.0 GB of system RAM, allocating roughly 1.3 GB per virtual core. Storage is bundled directly with an 80 GB local NVMe SSD, ensuring low-latency disk operations. It includes zero dedicated GPUs and does not come with complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring IPv6 or separate network routing configurations.

Benchmark results highlight solid baseline capabilities for single-threaded tasks alongside distinct constraints in parallel throughput. In stress-ng, single-core execution registers an average score of 2667.29, complemented by a Geekbench single-core result of 1469.0 and steady compression metrics in gzip and bzip3. Conversely, memory bandwidth benchmarks show uncached read and write speeds of 37.21 GB/sec and 20.78 GB/sec respectively, placing memory throughput in the lower quartile. Multi-core performance across Geekbench and PassMark reflects shared-vCPU limitations, where resource contention caps peak parallel output.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the cpx21 delivers strong economic efficiency for compute-light services requiring high-speed storage without large memory footprints. The bundled 80 GB NVMe disk provides substantial local storage density relative to its memory tier, offsetting lower memory bandwidth. Consequently, the instance is appropriate for utility jobs, development and staging servers, continuous integration worker nodes, low-traffic web hosting, and lightweight containerized services.
description: Hetzner Cloud cpx21 is an entry-level virtual server instance within the provider's Regular Purpose family, powered by the QEMU hypervisor on x86_64 architecture. The server provisions 3 shared AMD EPYC virtual cores clocked at 2.0 GHz, supported by 4.0 GB of system memory (1.3 GB per core) and 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It operates without an attached GPU or complimentary public IPv4 address. In benchmark testing, the cpx21 delivers average single-core and compression performance, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1469.0 and solid throughput in gzip and small-model inference tasks. However, multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth fall into the lower quartiles, reflecting shared resource constraints. Given its high storage-to-RAM ratio and multi-threaded CPU allocation at a budget-friendly tier, this server offers practical cost efficiency for lightweight microservices, testing and staging environments, low-traffic web applications, and utility background tasks.
